headline: High-risk orchestration-to-PDF workflow can leak data and cascade errors; prompt-injection risk is low because the pair lacks a direct shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kestra can read/write files and pass workflow inputs, while pdf.js only processes PDF files in a browser-based worker model. There is no documented direct shared channel or parser bridge between them, so prompt injection is possible mainly through manual file handoff or crafted PDFs, not by default.
conditions: IF Kestra writes attacker-controlled text into a PDF that pdf.js later opens as content to be interpreted by a human operator
IF an operator manually copies pdf.js output back into Kestra workflow definitions without review
mitigations: Use separate folders for Kestra inputs and pdf.js test PDFs
Require human review before copying PDF-derived text into workflows
Strip active content from PDFs before opening them
Disable any automation that converts PDF text into executable workflow steps
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to files passed between the tools

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, inputs, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, and has broad network egress plus file access. pdf.js reads PDF files locally and has no network egress, so the main leakage path is shared files or exported artifacts from Kestra into pdf.js. That exists in default orchestration setups and can expose sensitive document contents.
conditions: IF Kestra places sensitive artifacts in a directory that pdf.js can open
IF PDF contents processed by pdf.js are later written back into Kestra logs or artifacts
mitigations: Keep sensitive PDFs out of Kestra-accessible storage
Mount pdf.js on a read-only, separate workspace
Redact PDFs before orchestration
Turn off verbose logging for document-processing steps
requires-engineering: enforce per-tool data-loss-prevention checks

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances, and Kestra can write the filesystem while pdf.js reads PDF files from disk. Even though pdf.js is mostly read-only, shared workspace use can still create contention over the same files or artifacts, especially when Kestra rewrites inputs while pdf.js is processing them.
conditions: IF Kestra and pdf.js operate on the same directory at the same time
IF Kestra rewrites a PDF while pdf.js is reading it
mitigations: Use separate input and output directories
Serialize access to shared PDFs
Write Kestra outputs atomically to temp files first
Make pdf.js consume immutable copies
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra can generate workflow outputs, logs, and notifications that pdf.js may display or consume as documents, but pdf.js does not independently verify those contents. If operators treat rendered PDF text or extracted text as authoritative, errors from Kestra can cascade into downstream decisions or reports.
conditions: IF Kestra-generated text is embedded into PDFs that pdf.js renders without verification
IF an operator uses pdf.js output as the sole source for a downstream action
mitigations: Require source-document cross-checks before acting
Annotate extracted text with provenance
Use checksum validation on PDFs before processing
Limit pdf.js output to preview mode
requires-engineering: add verification gates between orchestration and document rendering

E_compliance.rationale: Kestra handles logs, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications with broad egress, while pdf.js processes PDF documents locally with no egress. That creates a compliance mismatch risk if regulated data is orchestrated by Kestra and then rendered or stored through pdf.js without aligned retention and residency controls.
conditions: IF regulated PDFs are routed through Kestra workflows and retained in shared storage
IF retention or residency rules differ between Kestra logs/artifacts and pdf.js outputs
mitigations: Classify PDFs before orchestration
Align retention settings across both tools
Store regulated documents in a dedicated compliant bucket
Disable unnecessary logging of document contents
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls per workflow
